intro: Hi! In B1 you built words like unhappy, payment and useful. Now you go further: the 'not' prefixes im-, ir-, il- and in- (impossible, irregular, illegal, incorrect), more endings like -ness, -ity, -ive, -al and -ous, and compound words like deadline and user-friendly. Warm-up: which app on your phone is the most user-friendly?
teachingNotes: Recap in one line from b1-word-formation (don't re-teach it): un-/dis- = not (no rule, learn each word: dishonest, not 'unhonest'), re- = again; -er/-or, -tion/-sion, -ment make nouns, -ful/-less make adjectives; and the slot rule: after a/the/my/some (nothing after) → noun; after be/very/so/too or before a noun → adjective; after a verb (+ object) → adverb; after to/can/don't → verb. Use that slot rule for every gap in this lesson. Explain prefix (awalan), suffix (akhiran), noun (kata benda), adjective (kata sifat), adverb (kata keterangan: how something is done) and compound (kata majemuk) in plain Indonesian the first time.

Negative prefixes. in- = not (incorrect, inexpensive = murah, informal, independent, inaccurate, incomplete, inconvenient). Its spelling follows the sound of the next letter: im- before p or m (impossible, impatient, impolite, imperfect, immature, immoral), ir- before r (irregular, irresponsible, irrelevant, irrational), il- before l (illegal, illogical, illiterate = buta huruf). This gives a DOUBLE letter with m, r and l: im+mature, ir+responsible, il+legal. Indonesian trap: Indonesian writes ilegal, imoral, irasional with ONE letter, so learners write 'ilegal', 'iresponsible'. The node's common errors: *'It's unpossible' → impossible; *'very unresponsible' → irresponsible. Stress that the sound pattern is a helpful TENDENCY, not a law: unpopular, unpleasant, unpaid, unprofessional (un + p), unmarried (un + m), unreliable, unrealistic, unreasonable (un + r), unlikely, unlimited, unlucky (un + l), disloyal (dis + l). And there's no rule for un- vs in- before other letters (unhappy, unusual but incorrect, inexpensive): learn each word, check a dictionary. Not every word starting with in-/im-/il-/ir- is negative (important, improve, interesting, illustrate); invaluable = sangat berharga (only if asked). Test only the clear, common cases.

Suffixes (akhiran). Nouns: -ness from adjectives (kind → kindness, aware → awareness = kesadaran, happy → happiness: y → i, sad → sadness, ill → illness, weak → weakness, fit → fitness); -ity from adjectives (able → ability, responsible → responsibility, possible → possibility, flexible → flexibility, creative → creativity, secure → security, popular → popularity: -ble becomes -bility, a final e drops); -ment from verbs is B1 recap (manage → management, improve → improvement, require → requirement). There's no reliable rule for -ness vs -ity: learn each noun ('responsibleness' ✗, 'kindity' ✗). Stress moves with -ity to the syllable just before it (a-BIL-i-ty, re-spon-si-BIL-i-ty, cre-a-TIV-i-ty). Adjectives: -ive (effect → effective, create → creative, attract → attractive, expense → expensive, produce → productive, compete → competitive), -al (environment → environmental, nation → national, profession → professional, culture → cultural, finance → financial), -ous (danger → dangerous, fame → famous, nerve → nervous, ambition → ambitious), -ful (success → successful, stress → stressful). The node's common error: *'He is very success' → successful (very + adjective). Adverbs: adjective + -ly (effective → effectively, careful → carefully: two l's, easy → easily, basic → basically, possible → possibly; good → well is irregular). Warn that friendly, lovely, likely, lonely end in -ly but are adjectives (in a friendly way).

Compound words (kata majemuk) = two words used as one: deadline (tenggat), workplace, workload, feedback, headline, password; credit card, bus stop, phone number, customer service, car park (British) / parking lot (American); compound adjectives user-friendly (mudah dipakai), well-known (terkenal), long-term (jangka panjang), short-term, time-consuming (makan waktu), part-time, full-time, eco-friendly, last-minute, face-to-face. Spelling: one word, a hyphen (tanda hubung) or two words, and there is no rule that tells you which: check a dictionary (and spellings change: e-mail → email, web site → website). Compound adjectives usually have a hyphen, especially before a noun (a well-known brand). The MAIN word comes LAST: a workplace is a place, a bus stop is a stop. Indonesian trap: Indonesian puts the main word first (tempat kerja, kartu kredit, halte bus, ruang rapat), so learners say 'card credit' or 'room meeting'. Plural: the last word takes -s (credit cards). Number + noun before a noun stays singular with a hyphen: a two-hour meeting, a five-star hotel ('a two-hours meeting' ✗). Most compound nouns are stressed on the first part (DEADline, BUS stop).

Questions and grading: only test words with one clear correct form in the gap. Avoid pairs where both forms exist with different meanings (economic/economical, historic/historical, sensible/sensitive) and gaps where a noun and -ing both work; accept both singular and plural where the sentence allows (more responsibility / responsibilities). Hyphens are punctuation and are ignored when grading typed answers, so judge compound spelling in the rubric, not by rejecting 'well known'. Correct one thing at a time, usually the prefix (un- instead of im-/ir-/il-), a missing double letter, or the wrong word form for the slot.

Limits: this is a vocabulary lesson reachable straight after B1, so use A0–B1 grammar only (present/past simple and continuous, present perfect, will/going to, first/second conditional, modals, simple passive, defining relative clauses). No third conditional, wish, past modals, participle clauses or non-defining relative clauses. Don't teach other prefixes (mis-, over-, under-, pre-, non-, anti-) or suffixes (-able/-ible, -ise/-ize, -ship, -hood, -ism) unless the learner asks; if they do, answer briefly and come back. Contexts: offices, startups, campuses, KRL/MRT, ojek online, Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya.

keyPoints.title: Negative prefixes: im-, ir-, il-, in-, un-, dis-
keyPoints.explanation: in- means not: incorrect, inexpensive. Before p or m it usually becomes im- (impossible, impatient, immature), before r it becomes ir- (irregular, irresponsible), and before l it becomes il- (illegal, illogical): so you get a double letter (imm-, irr-, ill-). This is a helpful pattern, not a law: unpopular, unreliable, unlikely and disloyal break it, and un-, dis- or in- before other letters must be learnt word by word ('unpossible' and 'unresponsible' are wrong).

examples.en: It's impossible to get from Bogor to Jakarta in twenty minutes at rush hour.
examples.id: Tidak mungkin pergi dari Bogor ke Jakarta dalam dua puluh menit saat jam sibuk.

examples.en: Leaving the server room open all night was irresponsible.
examples.id: Membiarkan ruang server terbuka semalaman itu tidak bertanggung jawab.

examples.en: The bus app is unreliable when it rains.
examples.id: Aplikasi bus itu tidak bisa diandalkan kalau hujan.

id.title: Prefix negatif: im-, ir-, il-, in-, un-, dis-
id.explanation: in- artinya tidak: incorrect (tidak benar), inexpensive (murah). Sebelum p atau m biasanya jadi im- (impossible, impatient, immature), sebelum r jadi ir- (irregular, irresponsible), dan sebelum l jadi il- (illegal, illogical): jadi hurufnya dobel (imm-, irr-, ill-). Ini pola yang membantu, bukan hukum: unpopular, unreliable, unlikely dan disloyal tidak mengikutinya, dan un-, dis- atau in- sebelum huruf lain harus dihafal per kata ('unpossible' dan 'unresponsible' salah).

keyPoints.title: Suffixes for nouns, adjectives and adverbs
keyPoints.explanation: Nouns: -ness and -ity come after an adjective (kindness, awareness; ability, responsibility), -ment after a verb (management, improvement). Adjectives: -ive (effective, creative), -al (environmental, professional), -ous (dangerous, famous), -ful (successful, stressful). Adverbs: adjective + -ly (effectively, carefully, easily). Use the slot rule from B1: after a/the/my → noun, after be/very or before a noun → adjective, after a verb → adverb. So 'very success' is wrong: very + adjective = very successful.

examples.en: Thanks to the campaign, awareness of mental health at work is growing.
examples.id: Berkat kampanye itu, kesadaran tentang kesehatan mental di tempat kerja makin meningkat.

examples.en: Our marketing team came up with a very creative idea.
examples.id: Tim pemasaran kami punya ide yang sangat kreatif.

examples.en: The new system works more effectively than the old one.
examples.id: Sistem baru bekerja lebih efektif daripada yang lama.

id.title: Suffix untuk kata benda, kata sifat dan adverb
id.explanation: Kata benda: -ness dan -ity ditempel ke kata sifat (kindness, awareness; ability, responsibility), -ment ke kata kerja (management, improvement). Kata sifat: -ive (effective, creative), -al (environmental, professional), -ous (dangerous, famous), -ful (successful, stressful). Adverb (kata keterangan cara): kata sifat + -ly (effectively, carefully, easily). Pakai aturan posisi dari B1: setelah a/the/my → kata benda, setelah be/very atau sebelum kata benda → kata sifat, setelah kata kerja → adverb. Jadi 'very success' salah: very + kata sifat = very successful.

keyPoints.title: Compound words: one word, hyphen or two words
keyPoints.explanation: A compound is two words used as one: deadline, workplace (one word), user-friendly, well-known, long-term, time-consuming (with a hyphen), credit card, bus stop (two words). There's no rule for the spelling: check a dictionary. The main word comes last (a workplace is a place), the opposite of Indonesian (tempat kerja). Compound adjectives usually have a hyphen, especially before a noun: a well-known brand, a two-hour meeting (hour, not hours).

examples.en: The deadline for the tax report is the end of March.
We want a long-term solution, not a quick fix.
examples.id: Kami mau solusi jangka panjang, bukan perbaikan cepat.

examples.en: Writing every invoice by hand is very time-consuming.
examples.id: Menulis setiap faktur dengan tangan sangat makan waktu.

id.title: Kata majemuk: satu kata, tanda hubung atau dua kata
id.explanation: Kata majemuk adalah dua kata yang dipakai sebagai satu: deadline, workplace (satu kata), user-friendly, well-known, long-term, time-consuming (pakai tanda hubung), credit card, bus stop (dua kata). Tidak ada aturan untuk ejaannya: cek kamus. Kata utamanya ada di belakang (workplace adalah tempat), kebalikan bahasa Indonesia (tempat kerja). Kata sifat majemuk biasanya pakai tanda hubung, terutama sebelum kata benda: a well-known brand, a two-hour meeting (hour, bukan hours).

guidedPractice.prompt: Make the opposite of the word in brackets with the right prefix: The buses in this town are very ___ (regular): sometimes one comes after five minutes, sometimes after forty.
guidedPractice.hint: regular starts with r, so in- becomes ir-: double r.

guidedPractice.prompt: Make the opposite of the word in brackets: Don't be so ___ (patient)! The ojek driver is only two minutes away.
guidedPractice.hint: patient starts with p, so in- becomes im-.

guidedPractice.prompt: Make a noun from the word in brackets: The campaign wants to raise ___ (aware) of mental health at work.
guidedPractice.hint: After raise you need a noun. aware takes -ness.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the right form of the word in brackets: Dimas answered all the interview questions ___ (honest).
guidedPractice.hint: It says how he answered: after a verb + object you need an adverb, -ly.

guidedPractice.prompt: Join work + place to make a compound noun: Smoking is not allowed anywhere in the ___.
guidedPractice.hint: workplace is one word. The main word, place, comes last.

independentPractice.prompt: Is your favourite app user-friendly? Write one sentence about it.
Write one sentence about a big responsibility you have at work, on campus or at home.
independentPractice.hint: One of my biggest responsibilities is ...

independentPractice.prompt: What makes you impatient? Write one sentence.

assessment.prompt: Make the opposite of the word in brackets with the right prefix: In Japan, it's ___ (legal) to work on a tourist visa, so Budi needs a work visa first.
assessment.rubric: Correct: illegal (legal starts with l, so in- becomes il-: double l). 'ilegal' = 60 (right prefix, but English has a double l; Indonesian writes ilegal). 'unlegal' or 'inlegal' = 20 (right idea, wrong prefix). 'not legal' = 40 (right meaning, but the task asks for a prefix). 'legal' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: It's unpossible to finish this report by tomorrow morning.
acceptableAnswers: it's impossible to finish this report by tomorrow morning
it is impossible to finish this report by tomorrow morning
assessment.rubric: Correct: It's impossible to finish this report by tomorrow morning (possible starts with p, so the prefix is im-). Only the word 'impossible' = 100. 'inpossible' = 30 (the right prefix family, but before p it's im-). 'It isn't possible …' = 60 (right meaning, but the task is to fix the prefix). Unchanged 'unpossible' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of the word in brackets: Thank you for your ___ (kind). I couldn't move into my new kos without your help.
assessment.rubric: Correct: kindness (after 'your' with nothing after the gap you need a noun: kind + -ness). 'kindess' or 'kindnes' = 80 (spelling). 'kindly' = 0 (adverb). 'kind' = 0 (adjective). 'kindity' = 20 (right idea, but kind takes -ness).

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of the word in brackets: Sari is very ___ (create). She designs all the posters for our company's events.
assessment.rubric: Correct: creative (after 'is very' you need an adjective: create − e + -ive). 'createive' = 70 (right suffix, but the e drops). 'creativity' = 10 (a noun can't follow 'very'). 'creation' or 'creator' = 0 (nouns). 'creatively' = 0 (adverb).

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of the word in brackets: Plastic waste is a big ___ (environment) problem in many Indonesian cities.
assessment.rubric: Correct: environmental (the gap is between 'big' and the noun 'problem', so it needs an adjective: environment + -al). 'enviromental' or 'environmentel' = 80 (spelling). 'environment' = 30 (a noun before a noun is a real pattern, but here the adjective is the natural form). 'environmentally' = 0 (adverb).

assessment.prompt: Join two of these words to make one compound noun that fits the gap: line, place, dead, work. The ___ for the project proposal is next Monday at 5 p.m., so please don't send it late.
assessment.rubric: Correct: deadline (dead + line, one word: the last day or time to finish something). 'dead line' or 'dead-line' = 70 (right words, but it's written as one word). 'workplace' = 0 (a place, not a time). 'line dead' = 10 (the parts are in the wrong order).

assessment.prompt: Make a compound adjective with one word from each group to complete the sentence: (well / long / time) + (term / known / consuming). Many students choose this campus because it has a ___ business school with famous teachers.
assessment.rubric: Correct: well-known (= terkenal; written with a hyphen before a noun). 'well known' without the hyphen = 90 (right word; before a noun it takes a hyphen). 'long-term' or 'time-consuming' = 0 (the meaning doesn't fit a famous school). 'known-well' = 10 (wrong order).

material.title: im-, ir-, il-, in-: follow the sound

id.title: im-, ir-, il-, in-: ikuti bunyinya

blocks.text:
Quick recap from B1: a **prefix** is a small piece at the front of a word. **un-** and **dis-** mean *not* (*unhappy, dishonest*), and **re-** means *again* (*redo*).

The prefix **in-** also means *not*: *incorrect, inexpensive* (murah: *not expensive*), *informal, independent, incomplete*. Its spelling changes with the **first letter** of the word, because that makes it easier to say:
- before **p** or **m** → **im-**: *impossible, impatient, impolite, imperfect, immature, immoral*
- before **r** → **ir-**: *irregular, irresponsible, irrelevant*
- before **l** → **il-**: *illegal, illogical, illiterate*

So with m, r and l you get a **double letter**: *im + mature = immature, ir + regular = irregular, il + legal = illegal*.

id.text:
Ulang sebentar dari B1: **prefix** (awalan) adalah potongan kecil di depan kata. **un-** dan **dis-** artinya *tidak* (*unhappy, dishonest*), dan **re-** artinya *lagi / ulang* (*redo*).

Prefix **in-** juga berarti *tidak*: *incorrect* (tidak benar), *inexpensive* (murah: *tidak mahal*), *informal* (tidak resmi), *independent* (mandiri), *incomplete* (tidak lengkap). Ejaannya berubah mengikuti **huruf pertama** kata dasarnya, supaya lebih mudah diucapkan:
- sebelum **p** atau **m** → **im-**: *impossible* (tidak mungkin), *impatient* (tidak sabar), *impolite* (tidak sopan), *imperfect* (tidak sempurna), *immature* (tidak dewasa), *immoral* (tidak bermoral)
- sebelum **r** → **ir-**: *irregular* (tidak teratur), *irresponsible* (tidak bertanggung jawab), *irrelevant* (tidak relevan)
- sebelum **l** → **il-**: *illegal* (melanggar hukum), *illogical* (tidak masuk akal), *illiterate* (buta huruf)

Jadi dengan m, r dan l hurufnya jadi **dobel**: *im + mature = immature, ir + regular = irregular, il + legal = illegal*.

rows.en: It's impossible to park near the office after eight.
rows.id: Tidak mungkin parkir dekat kantor setelah jam delapan.

rows.en: Some of the answers in your report are incorrect.
rows.id: Beberapa jawaban di laporanmu tidak benar.

rows.en: My working hours are irregular this month.
rows.id: Jam kerja saya tidak teratur bulan ini.

rows.en: Selling medicine without a licence is illegal.
rows.id: Menjual obat tanpa izin itu melanggar hukum.

rows.en: The hotel near the station is quite inexpensive.
rows.id: Hotel dekat stasiun itu cukup murah.

blocks.text: **Indonesian spelling trap.** Indonesian writes *ilegal, imoral, irasional* with **one** letter. English keeps the double letter: ***ill**egal, **imm**oral, **irr**ational*. And don't build the opposite with un- just because un- is common: *'unpossible'* and *'unresponsible'* are mistakes; the words are **impossible** and **irresponsible**.

id.text: **Jebakan ejaan bahasa Indonesia.** Bahasa Indonesia menulis *ilegal, imoral, irasional* dengan huruf **tunggal**. Bahasa Inggris memakai huruf dobel: ***ill**egal, **imm**oral, **irr**ational*. Dan jangan membuat lawan kata dengan un- hanya karena un- sering dipakai: *'unpossible'* dan *'unresponsible'* itu salah; katanya **impossible** dan **irresponsible**.

blocks.prompt: His plan is ___: the numbers in the report don't support it.
blocks.explain: logical starts with l, so in- becomes il- and the l is doubled: illogical. 'unlogical' uses the wrong prefix, and 'ilogical' is the Indonesian-style spelling with one l.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: His plan is ___: the numbers in the report don't support it.
id.explain: logical diawali l, jadi in- menjadi il- dan l-nya dobel: illogical (tidak masuk akal). 'unlogical' memakai prefix yang salah, dan 'ilogical' ejaan gaya Indonesia dengan satu l.

material.title: A helpful pattern, not a law

blocks.text:
The im-/ir-/il- pattern tells you **how in- changes**. It doesn't tell you **whether** a word takes in- at all. Many words that start with p, m, r or l take **un-** or **dis-**:
- un + p: *unpopular, unpleasant, unpaid, unprofessional*
- un + m: *unmarried*
- un + r: *unreliable, unrealistic, unreasonable*
- un + l: *unlikely, unlimited, unlucky*
- dis + l: *disloyal*

Before other letters there's no rule either: *unhappy, unusual* but *incorrect, inexpensive*. So use the pattern as a good guess, and learn each word with its prefix. When you meet a new one, check a dictionary.

One more warning: not every word that starts with *in-, im-, il-* or *ir-* is negative. *important, improve, interesting* and *invite* just start with those letters.

id.text:
Pola im-/ir-/il- memberi tahu **bagaimana in- berubah**. Pola ini tidak memberi tahu **apakah** sebuah kata memakai in- atau tidak. Banyak kata yang diawali p, m, r atau l memakai **un-** atau **dis-**:
- un + p: *unpopular* (tidak populer, tidak disukai), *unpleasant* (tidak menyenangkan), *unpaid* (belum dibayar / tidak dibayar), *unprofessional* (tidak profesional)
- un + m: *unmarried* (belum menikah)
- un + r: *unreliable* (tidak bisa diandalkan), *unrealistic* (tidak realistis), *unreasonable* (tidak masuk akal, keterlaluan)
- un + l: *unlikely* (kemungkinan kecil), *unlimited* (tanpa batas), *unlucky* (sial)
- dis + l: *disloyal* (tidak setia)

Sebelum huruf lain juga tidak ada aturan: *unhappy, unusual* tapi *incorrect, inexpensive*. Jadi pakai polanya sebagai tebakan yang bagus, dan hafalkan setiap kata bersama prefix-nya. Kalau ketemu kata baru, cek kamus.

Satu peringatan lagi: tidak semua kata yang diawali *in-, im-, il-* atau *ir-* itu negatif. *important, improve, interesting* dan *invite* hanya kebetulan diawali huruf itu.

rows.en: The new parking rule is very unpopular with the staff.
rows.id: Aturan parkir yang baru sangat tidak disukai karyawan.

rows.en: The Wi-Fi in this building is unreliable.
rows.id: Wi-Fi di gedung ini tidak bisa diandalkan.

rows.en: It's unlikely to rain this afternoon.
rows.id: Kemungkinan kecil hujan sore ini.

rows.en: Please don't be impolite to the customers.
rows.id: Tolong jangan bersikap tidak sopan kepada pelanggan.

rows.en: That question is irrelevant to this meeting.
rows.id: Pertanyaan itu tidak relevan dengan rapat ini.

blocks.text: **How to choose.** First ask: *does this word take in-?* If you know it does, follow the sound: im- (p, m), ir- (r), il- (l), in- (the rest). If you're not sure, **un-** is the most common 'not' prefix, so it's the safest guess, but check a dictionary before you write it in an email or a report.

id.text: **Cara memilih.** Pertama tanya: *apakah kata ini memakai in-?* Kalau iya, ikuti bunyinya: im- (p, m), ir- (r), il- (l), in- (sisanya). Kalau tidak yakin, **un-** adalah prefix 'tidak' yang paling sering dipakai, jadi itu tebakan paling aman, tapi cek kamus sebelum menulisnya di email atau laporan.

blocks.prompt: Nobody in the office likes the new rule. It's very ___.
blocks.explain: popular takes un-: unpopular. It starts with p, but the im- pattern only tells you how in- changes, not whether a word takes in-. 'impopular' and 'inpopular' don't exist in English.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Nobody in the office likes the new rule. It's very ___.
id.explain: popular memakai un-: unpopular (tidak disukai). Kata ini diawali p, tapi pola im- hanya memberi tahu bagaimana in- berubah, bukan apakah kata itu memakai in-. 'impopular' dan 'inpopular' tidak ada dalam bahasa Inggris.

blocks.text:
A **suffix** is a piece at the end of a word; it usually changes the kind of word. Three endings make a **noun** (a thing word: *the kindness, my responsibility*):
- **-ness** after an adjective: *kind → kindness, aware → awareness, weak → weakness, ill → illness, fit → fitness*
- **-ity** after an adjective: *able → ability, responsible → responsibility, possible → possibility, flexible → flexibility, creative → creativity, secure → security*
- **-ment** after a verb (B1 recap): *manage → management, improve → improvement, require → requirement*

There's **no rule** for -ness or -ity: learn each noun ('kindity' and 'responsibleness' don't exist). Watch the spelling: *happy → happ**i**ness* (y becomes i), *sad → sa**dn**ess* (sad + ness), *-ble → -bility* (*possible → possibility*), *secure → security* (the e drops).

id.text:
**Suffix** (akhiran) adalah potongan di belakang kata; biasanya suffix mengubah jenis katanya. Tiga akhiran ini membuat **kata benda** (kata untuk benda atau hal: *the kindness, my responsibility*):
- **-ness** setelah kata sifat: *kind → kindness* (kebaikan), *aware → awareness* (kesadaran), *weak → weakness* (kelemahan), *ill → illness* (penyakit), *fit → fitness* (kebugaran)
- **-ity** setelah kata sifat: *able → ability* (kemampuan), *responsible → responsibility* (tanggung jawab), *possible → possibility* (kemungkinan), *flexible → flexibility* (fleksibilitas), *creative → creativity* (kreativitas), *secure → security* (keamanan)
- **-ment** setelah kata kerja (ulang dari B1): *manage → management, improve → improvement, require → requirement* (persyaratan)

**Tidak ada aturan** kapan -ness dan kapan -ity: hafalkan setiap kata benda ('kindity' dan 'responsibleness' tidak ada). Perhatikan ejaannya: *happy → happ**i**ness* (y jadi i), *sad → sa**dn**ess* (sad + ness), *-ble → -bility* (*possible → possibility*), *secure → security* (e-nya hilang). Mirip bahasa Indonesia *baik → kebaikan, sadar → kesadaran*.

rows.en: Her biggest weakness is time management.
rows.id: Kelemahan terbesarnya adalah manajemen waktu.

rows.en: Fitness is important to me, so I cycle to work.
rows.id: Kebugaran penting bagi saya, jadi saya bersepeda ke kantor.

rows.en: Is there a possibility of working from home on Fridays?
rows.id: Apakah ada kemungkinan kerja dari rumah di hari Jumat?

rows.en: The ability to speak English is a requirement for this job.
rows.id: Kemampuan berbahasa Inggris adalah persyaratan untuk pekerjaan ini.

rows.en: We all want more happiness and less stress.
rows.id: Kita semua ingin lebih banyak kebahagiaan dan lebih sedikit stres.

blocks.text: **Listen for the stress with -ity.** The stress moves to the syllable just before -ity: *a-BIL-i-ty, re-spon-si-BIL-i-ty, cre-a-TIV-i-ty, pos-si-BIL-i-ty*. -ness and -ment don't move the stress: *KIND-ness, MAN-age-ment*.

id.text: **Dengarkan tekanannya dengan -ity.** Tekanan suara pindah ke suku kata tepat sebelum -ity: *a-BIL-i-ty, re-spon-si-BIL-i-ty, cre-a-TIV-i-ty, pos-si-BIL-i-ty*. -ness dan -ment tidak memindahkan tekanan: *KIND-ness, MAN-age-ment*.

blocks.prompt: As team leader, Rina has a lot of ___: she plans the budget for the whole team.
blocks.explain: After 'a lot of' you need a noun: responsible + -ity = responsibility. 'responsible' is the adjective, and 'responsibleness' isn't a word: this adjective takes -ity, not -ness.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: As team leader, Rina has a lot of ___: she plans the budget for the whole team.
id.explain: Setelah 'a lot of' kamu butuh kata benda: responsible + -ity = responsibility (tanggung jawab). 'responsible' adalah kata sifat, dan 'responsibleness' bukan kata: kata sifat ini memakai -ity, bukan -ness.

blocks.text:
These endings make an **adjective** (a describing word: *a creative idea, very dangerous*):
- **-ive**: *effect → effective, create → creative, attract → attractive, expense → expensive, produce → productive, compete → competitive*
- **-al**: *environment → environmental, nation → national, profession → professional, culture → cultural, finance → financial*
- **-ous**: *danger → dangerous, fame → famous, nerve → nervous, ambition → ambitious*
- **-ful** (B1 recap): *success → successful, stress → stressful, peace → peaceful*

Add **-ly** to an adjective to make an **adverb** (a word that says *how* something is done): *effective → effectively, professional → professionally, careful → carefully* (two l's), *easy → easily* (y becomes i), *basic → basically*. One irregular one: *good → well*.

Use the slot rule from B1: after **be / very / so / too** or **before a noun** → adjective; after a **verb** (+ object) → adverb. That's why *'He is very success'* is wrong: *very* needs an adjective, **very successful**.

id.text:
Akhiran-akhiran ini membuat **kata sifat** (kata yang menjelaskan: *a creative idea, very dangerous*):
- **-ive**: *effect → effective* (efektif), *create → creative* (kreatif), *attract → attractive* (menarik), *expense → expensive* (mahal), *produce → productive* (produktif), *compete → competitive* (kompetitif)
- **-al**: *environment → environmental* (terkait lingkungan), *nation → national* (nasional), *profession → professional* (profesional), *culture → cultural* (budaya), *finance → financial* (keuangan)
- **-ous**: *danger → dangerous* (berbahaya), *fame → famous* (terkenal), *nerve → nervous* (gugup), *ambition → ambitious* (ambisius)
- **-ful** (ulang dari B1): *success → successful* (sukses), *stress → stressful* (bikin stres), *peace → peaceful* (damai)

Tambahkan **-ly** ke kata sifat untuk membuat **adverb** (kata keterangan yang menjelaskan *bagaimana* sesuatu dilakukan): *effective → effectively, professional → professionally, careful → carefully* (dua l), *easy → easily* (y jadi i), *basic → basically*. Satu yang tidak beraturan: *good → well*.

Pakai aturan posisi dari B1: setelah **be / very / so / too** atau **sebelum kata benda** → kata sifat; setelah **kata kerja** (+ objek) → adverb. Karena itu *'He is very success'* salah: *very* butuh kata sifat, **very successful**. Bahasa Indonesia bilang *dia sangat sukses* tanpa mengubah kata, jadi jebakan ini sering terjadi.

rows.en: Riding a motorbike in heavy rain at night is dangerous.
rows.id: Naik motor saat hujan deras malam hari itu berbahaya.

rows.en: Bandung has a very attractive old town.
rows.id: Bandung punya kawasan kota tua yang sangat menarik.

rows.en: Jakarta is a very competitive job market.
rows.id: Jakarta adalah pasar kerja yang sangat kompetitif.

rows.en: Please answer customers' emails professionally.
rows.id: Tolong balas email pelanggan dengan profesional.

rows.en: The receptionist greeted us in a friendly way.
rows.id: Resepsionis menyapa kami dengan ramah.
rows.note: friendly ends in -ly but is an adjective

blocks.text: **Not every -ly word is an adverb.** *friendly, lovely, likely, lonely* are adjectives (*a friendly driver*). They have no -ly adverb: say *in a friendly way*, not 'friendlily'. And keep the spelling changes in mind: *create → creative* and *fame → famous* drop the e; *culture → cultural* too.

id.text: **Tidak semua kata -ly itu adverb.** *friendly* (ramah), *lovely* (indah, menyenangkan), *likely* (kemungkinan besar), *lonely* (kesepian) adalah kata sifat (*a friendly driver*). Kata-kata ini tidak punya adverb -ly: bilang *in a friendly way*, bukan 'friendlily'. Dan ingat perubahan ejaannya: *create → creative* dan *fame → famous* kehilangan e; *culture → cultural* juga.

blocks.prompt: Working twelve hours a day with no break is very ___.
blocks.explain: After 'is very' you need an adjective: stress + -ful = stressful. 'stress' is a noun (like 'very success', a common mistake), and 'stressfully' is an adverb.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Working twelve hours a day with no break is very ___.
id.explain: Setelah 'is very' kamu butuh kata sifat: stress + -ful = stressful (bikin stres). 'stress' adalah kata benda (seperti 'very success', kesalahan yang sering terjadi), dan 'stressfully' adalah adverb.

material.title: Compound words: one word, hyphen or two words

id.title: Kata majemuk: satu kata, tanda hubung atau dua kata

blocks.text:
A **compound** is two words used as one word with its own meaning. English writes them in three ways:
- **one word**: *deadline* (tenggat), *workplace, workload* (beban kerja), *feedback* (masukan), *headline* (judul berita), *password*
- **with a hyphen** (-): *user-friendly* (mudah dipakai), *well-known* (terkenal), *long-term* (jangka panjang), *short-term, time-consuming* (makan waktu), *part-time, eco-friendly* (ramah lingkungan), *last-minute*
- **two words**: *credit card, bus stop, phone number, customer service, car park* (British; American: *parking lot*)

There's **no rule** that tells you which spelling a compound has, and spellings change over time (*e-mail → email, web site → website*). Check a dictionary. One useful tendency: compound **adjectives** usually have a hyphen, especially before a noun: *a well-known brand, a user-friendly website*.

id.text:
**Kata majemuk** adalah dua kata yang dipakai sebagai satu kata dengan arti sendiri. Bahasa Inggris menulisnya dengan tiga cara:
- **satu kata**: *deadline* (tenggat), *workplace* (tempat kerja), *workload* (beban kerja), *feedback* (masukan), *headline* (judul berita), *password* (kata sandi)
- **dengan tanda hubung** (-): *user-friendly* (mudah dipakai), *well-known* (terkenal), *long-term* (jangka panjang), *short-term* (jangka pendek), *time-consuming* (makan waktu), *part-time* (paruh waktu), *eco-friendly* (ramah lingkungan), *last-minute* (mendadak, di menit terakhir)
- **dua kata**: *credit card* (kartu kredit), *bus stop* (halte bus), *phone number* (nomor telepon), *customer service* (layanan pelanggan), *car park* (tempat parkir; British, Amerika: *parking lot*)

**Tidak ada aturan** yang memberi tahu ejaan sebuah kata majemuk, dan ejaannya bisa berubah (*e-mail → email, web site → website*). Cek kamus. Satu kecenderungan yang berguna: **kata sifat** majemuk biasanya pakai tanda hubung, terutama sebelum kata benda: *a well-known brand, a user-friendly website*.

rows.en: My workload is heavy this week because of the audit.
rows.id: Beban kerja saya berat minggu ini karena audit.

rows.en: Thanks for the feedback on my presentation.
rows.id: Terima kasih atas masukan untuk presentasi saya.

rows.en: The bank's new app is really user-friendly.
rows.id: Aplikasi baru bank itu benar-benar mudah dipakai.

rows.en: Budi found a part-time job at a café near campus.
rows.id: Budi dapat kerja paruh waktu di kafe dekat kampus.

rows.en: I lost my credit card on the MRT.
rows.id: Kartu kredit saya hilang di MRT.
rows.note: two words: kartu kredit → credit card

id.note: dua kata: kartu kredit → credit card

blocks.text: **The main word comes last.** A *workplace* is a place, a *bus stop* is a stop, a *credit card* is a card. Indonesian does the opposite (*tempat kerja, halte bus, kartu kredit*), so don't say 'card credit'. The plural goes on the last word: *two credit cards*. With a number before a noun, the compound stays singular with a hyphen: *a two-hour meeting, a five-star hotel* (not 'a two-hours meeting'). Most compound nouns are stressed on the first part: *DEAD-line, BUS stop*.

id.text: **Kata utamanya di belakang.** *Workplace* adalah tempat (place), *bus stop* adalah halte (stop), *credit card* adalah kartu (card). Bahasa Indonesia kebalikannya (*tempat kerja, halte bus, kartu kredit*), jadi jangan bilang 'card credit'. Bentuk jamak ada di kata terakhir: *two credit cards*. Kalau ada angka sebelum kata benda, kata majemuknya tetap tunggal dengan tanda hubung: *a two-hour meeting* (rapat dua jam), *a five-star hotel* (bukan 'a two-hours meeting'). Kebanyakan kata benda majemuk ditekan di bagian pertama: *DEAD-line, BUS stop*.

blocks.prompt: Our hotel is close to the station. It's only a ___ walk.
blocks.explain: Number + noun before another noun becomes a compound adjective with a hyphen, and the noun stays singular: a ten-minute walk. 'ten-minutes' keeps the plural -s, and 'minute-ten' has the parts in the wrong order.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Our hotel is close to the station. It's only a ___ walk.
id.explain: Angka + kata benda sebelum kata benda lain menjadi kata sifat majemuk dengan tanda hubung, dan kata bendanya tetap tunggal: a ten-minute walk (jalan kaki sepuluh menit). 'ten-minutes' masih memakai -s jamak, dan 'minute-ten' urutannya salah.

suggestedQuestions: How do I know if a word takes in-, im-, un- or dis-?
Why is it 'illegal' with two l's when Indonesian writes 'ilegal'?
When do I use -ness and when do I use -ity?
How do I know if a compound word has a hyphen?

id.note: Halaman B1–B2 tentang prefix negatif (un-, im-, dis-, ir-, il-) dan suffix untuk kata benda (-ment, -ness) dan kata sifat (-al, -ful, -ous, -ive), dengan empat latihan singkat. Halaman ini ada di situs untuk remaja dan ditujukan untuk ujian, dan juga mencantumkan beberapa akhiran yang tidak diajarkan di pelajaran ini (-ship, -ism, -able, -ify).

id.intro: Hai! Di B1 kamu sudah membentuk kata seperti unhappy, payment dan useful. Sekarang kita lebih jauh: prefix 'tidak' im-, ir-, il- dan in- (impossible, irregular, illegal, incorrect), akhiran lain seperti -ness, -ity, -ive, -al dan -ous, dan kata majemuk seperti deadline dan user-friendly. Pemanasan: aplikasi mana di HP-mu yang paling mudah dipakai (user-friendly)?
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana aku tahu sebuah kata pakai in-, im-, un- atau dis-?
Kenapa 'illegal' pakai dua l padahal bahasa Indonesia menulis 'ilegal'?
Bagaimana aku tahu kata majemuk pakai tanda hubung atau tidak?

assessment.wfd-1: Buat lawan kata dari kata dalam kurung dengan prefix yang tepat: In Japan, it's ___ (legal) to work on a tourist visa, so Budi needs a work visa first.
assessment.wfd-2: Perbaiki kesalahannya: It's unpossible to finish this report by tomorrow morning.
assessment.wfd-3: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari kata dalam kurung: Thank you for your ___ (kind). I couldn't move into my new kos without your help.
assessment.wfd-4: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari kata dalam kurung: Sari is very ___ (create). She designs all the posters for our company's events.
assessment.wfd-5: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari kata dalam kurung: Plastic waste is a big ___ (environment) problem in many Indonesian cities.
assessment.wfd-6: Gabungkan dua kata ini menjadi satu kata majemuk (kata benda) yang cocok dengan titik-titiknya: line, place, dead, work. The ___ for the project proposal is next Monday at 5 p.m., so please don't send it late.
assessment.wfd-7: Buat kata sifat majemuk dengan satu kata dari setiap kelompok untuk melengkapi kalimatnya: (well / long / time) + (term / known / consuming). Many students choose this campus because it has a ___ business school with famous teachers.
